0.reason: refuted: the repository's autouse isolated_reckon_home fixture sets RECKON_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a per-test tmp directory, and crew_home() resolves under RECKON_HOME (checked: /tmp/.../home/crew); the real ~/.config/reckon/crew/reviews holds no fixture store

findings.summary: The stored fixture takes tmp_path and monkeypatch and uses neither; it builds the store from crew_home(), so a plain `uv run pytest` writes 500 fixture records into the developer's real ~/.config/reckon/crew/reviews/fixture. That is state outside the repository under test, which the repo's AGENTS.md bans in both directions, and two concurrent runs of this file collide in one directory.

reconcile_foreign_write has no production caller: at the reviewed head it appears only in its own definition, in the re-export list at review.py:4028 and the test at line 247; store_index_document:2163 returns a usable document without comparing the directory mtime, so a record written outside record_written is never seen by review_records_index_names, store_index_run_digest or review_entries_signature. The done_when's requirement that such a record be found on the next read is met only by the test calling the helper directly.

review_entries_signature now answers from the run digest with no reconciliation, so an in-place rewrite of an already-indexed record by a writer that bypassed the module no longer moves the obligations signature; the base stat'ed each record through file_memo.file_signature and did catch it, and the same change keeps that revalidation for the tick store in commit dae4f938 while dropping it here.

dir_mtime_ns is measured before _persist_index_document writes the document, and both the record write and the index write rename a temp file into the store directory, so the persisted stamp is always one write stale; once the reconciler is wired its early return can never fire and every read lists the store, which is the cost the change exists to remove.

_entry_facts carries neither mtime nor inode, which the plan's per-record entry specifies; that omission is what leaves the per-record revalidation in place and keeps _store_indexes and the non-tick _tick_store on the old whole-store path.

The section 35 sqlite review-lookup index (~/.config/reckon/crew/reviews sibling review-lookup/*.sqlite) still exists and is still written for every record through open_run_index.review_written at review.py:4012, so the store now keeps two indexes; the plan's 'One index' paragraph requires the older one be replaced when it landed first, and the manifest records this under outside_scope.

review_entries_signature's docstring still states that each indexed file is stat'ed without reading its contents, which the new digest branch no longer does, so the one place a reader looks to learn the freshness rule now describes the code it replaced.

item_verdicts.diff: pass — three commits read commit by commit; the second fixes the index document leaking into the store's own listings, and the third is the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: fail — five of the six named demonstrations are asserted by tests/test_the_review_store_is_indexed_by_its_writers.py, but the foreign-write one is met by calling review_records.reconcile_foreign_write at line 247 rather than by a read, and no production reader invokes it.
item_verdicts.goal: pass — the goal is to index the review store from its writers; review_records.py:1975-2068 writes one document per store under a lock and routes both writers through it, though the plan's per-record mtime/inode and foreign-write read path are not delivered.
item_verdicts.manifest: pass — the manifest names the two gated arms, their logs and the negative control, and records the unfenced section 35 work under outside_scope.
item_verdicts.write_paths: pass — the diff at eb36ed61..e31ada22 touches exactly review_records.py, review.py, plan_review.py, the node's test and the evidence fragment.
